title: Reported reasons for monthly SNAP entry and exit are heterogeneous
source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent reference-month SNAP transition with a classified recorded reason

observations.period: 2024; SNAP no -> yes; recorded entry reason

denominator.unit: classified person transition pairs with a valid recorded entry reason

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive reason distribution using WPFINWGT from the first month and REPWGT1–REPWGT240; reason is recorded at the transition-linked month.
observations.uncertainty: Entry transitions are rare; 217 classified pairs are a subset of 437 entry pairs. Intervals describe sampling uncertainty and do not establish cause or program impact.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt with a valid recorded entry reason.
observations.counterinterpretation: A recorded reason can summarize multiple conditions and does not identify the dated event, benefit adequacy, administrative responsibility, or unobserved alternative.

observations.period: 2024; SNAP yes -> no; recorded exit reason

denominator.unit: classified person transition pairs with a valid recorded exit reason

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive reason distribution using WPFINWGT from the first month and REPWGT1–REPWGT240; exit reason is recorded at the transition-linked month.
observations.uncertainty: Exit transitions are rare; 188 classified pairs are a subset of 387 exit pairs. Intervals describe sampling uncertainty and do not establish that exit caused restored security or income.
observations.subgroup: Persons exiting reported SNAP receipt with a valid recorded exit reason.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exit can reflect income, renewal, household, reporting, administrative, or timing changes; the large other category prevents a complete mechanism ranking.

related_sources.claim: The reproduction audit preserves the input hashes, row counts, matched reason pairs, and Fay-BRR method.

boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive distribution of respondent-recorded reasons around selected monthly SNAP transitions. It does not establish a causal event, benefit adequacy, notice or remedy failure, household benefit spell, food or housing outcome, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Classified reason universes are smaller than all transition universes, and the entry and exit reason taxonomies are not interchangeable.
